newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Consgold says Davyhurst gold mine open.
newsitem.headline: Consgold says Davyhurst gold mine open.

text.p: Western Australia gold miner Consolidated Gold NL said on Monday that its 120,000 ounce-a-year Davyhurst mine in the Riverina region has been commissioned and should reach full production next month.

"Commissioning of the Davyhurst mill is proceeding smoothly, with final performance testing currently underway and the plant expected to reach its (annualised) design throughput of 1.3 million tonnes per annum during July," managing director Collis Thorp said in a statement. Cash production costs have been budgeted for A$340 an ounce.
Ore feed from the plant will come from the underground Lights of Israel operation, the new Waihi open pit and existing oxide stockpiles, Thorp said.
The Lights of Israel operation, bought from Aberfoyle Ltd in October, has exceeded expectations and reached about 50,000 tonnes a month instead of the forecast 40,000 tonnes.
Encouraging preliminary results have also been seen from a new drilling programme at Mulline. A diamond drilling programme will start as soon as a rig become available, Thorp said.
Exploration at the Waihi pit will continue after work identified potentially significant underground ore shoots. An annual budget of A$3 million has been set for exploration.
Production will also continue for the next two to three months at Consgold's Kookynie mine, where testing will shift from surface oxide resources to larger primary bedrock deposits, Thorp said.
